note: One core release. The daemon `axiom-graphd` and the installation CLI `axiom` are built from one Rust workspace, one version and one revision, and are published together. There is no separate `axiom-bootstrap` release component. This file declares that release and records honestly what this workstream verified and what it did not: it is a declaration, not a publication record, and it claims no artifact that was not built.

release.name: axiom-core
release.revision_note: The release gate is closed for this workstream, so no commit is pinned and no tag is created. An authorized maintenance workflow replaces `unpinned` with the 40-character build revision and re-runs tests/core_manifest.py.
release.bootstrap_note: Bootstrap and installer behaviour live inside this same workspace and ship in this same core release; there is no second component, no second version and no second publication for them.

compatibility.notes: The daemon and the CLI share one core version and one graph/control/queue schema set, so a mixed daemon/CLI pair from the same release is the only supported combination; see crates/axiom/src/version.rs, which this file is checked against by tests/core_manifest.py.

signature.note: Signing is an authorized maintenance step and is not performed here. A release is not publishable while any signature state is `required` and no key id is recorded.

publication.reason: This workstream keeps the release gate closed: no tag, no release, no publish. Publication is a separate authorized maintenance action.
